reference: GNU coreutils tr 9.x under LC_ALL=C provides independent ASCII ROT13 and fixed Caesar transliteration maps. GNU coreutils file commands provide the reference side for a private relative-path file lifecycle and tree comparison. The other runnable expectations are contract checks: Bash type/help metadata, mathematically enumerated primes, English cardinal spelling, standard International Morse code, and the documented invalid-game usage status. No bsdgames result is used to construct an expectation.
coverage: Bash builtin type/help metadata is present.
ROT13 stdin filtering preserves binary nonletters, NUL, high bytes, and a missing final newline against GNU tr.
ROT13 argument joining and newline behavior are compared against GNU tr.
An explicit positive Caesar shift is compared against GNU tr on binary stdin.
Prime range lower and upper boundaries are checked against a hand-enumerated mathematical result.
Negative grouped and zero integer spelling are checked against the English cardinal contract.
Morse letters, a digit, punctuation skipping, and word separation are checked against International Morse code.
Unknown-game dispatch returns a usage failure without stdout.
ROT13 consumes a moved file after ordinary private file setup; tree comparison covers setup effects without inflating game operation counts.
exclusions: No full upstream BSD-games conformance is claimed; the binary contains bounded adapters and contracts vary by game.
Interactive terminal gameplay is deferred because this runner has no PTY or terminal-driver fixture mode.
External game data, score/state persistence, and broad adapter coverage are not exercised.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata must identify bsdgames as a builtin, and the documented loadable help topic must be available.
Compare the byte-stream filter against GNU tr, including NUL, 0xff, CR/LF, punctuation, and input without a final newline.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bsdgames) == builtin ]]; then
  printf '\000Az Nn! \377\r\nlastZ' | bsdgames rot13
else
  printf '\000Az Nn! \377\r\nlastZ' | tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m'
fi

cases.purpose: Compare argument joining with spaces and the required trailing newline against GNU tr on the equivalent text stream.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bsdgames) == builtin ]]; then
  bsdgames rot13 'Hello,' 'WORLD!' '123'
else
  printf '%s\n' 'Hello, WORLD! 123' | tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m'
fi

cases.purpose: Compare an explicit Caesar shift of five on stdin against GNU tr's independently written alphabet mapping, preserving nonletters and binary endpoints.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bsdgames) == builtin ]]; then
  printf '\000Az, Hello! \377' | bsdgames caesar 5
else
  printf '\000Az, Hello! \377' | tr 'A-Za-z' 'F-ZA-Ef-za-e'
fi

cases.purpose: Compare ROT13 of a moved private file with GNU tr, with ordinary file operations as setup. Tree comparison additionally checks setup contents/modes/links; these are not separate bsdgames operations.
cases.script:
mkdir box
touch box/temporary
printf 'Az, file!\n' > box/source
chmod 640 box/source
cp box/source box/copy
ln box/source box/hard
ln -s source box/symbolic
mv box/copy box/moved
rm box/temporary
if [[ $(type -t bsdgames) == builtin ]]; then
  bsdgames rot13 < box/moved > box/output
else
  tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m' < box/moved > box/output
fi

cases.purpose: Check that a range beginning below the first prime clamps to two and includes a prime at the upper endpoint; the expected list is independently enumerated by divisibility.
Check the documented English cardinal spelling for a negative value with omitted zero groups and for zero.
cases.stdout:
minus two million forty thousand thirty
zero

cases.purpose: Check standard International Morse encodings for SOS and digit 2, a slash word separator, punctuation skipping, and output newline behavior without a trailing input newline.
An unknown game name must be rejected as a usage error, emit no stdout, and provide a diagnostic.
Interactive game controls and terminal redraw behavior need a real bounded terminal session.
Check empty input, then distinct regular-file inputs on repeated calls in one shell against GNU tr.
cases.script: printf '' > empty; printf 'Hello' > first; printf 'World\n' > second; if [[ $(type -t bsdgames) == builtin ]]; then bsdgames rot13 < empty; bsdgames rot13 < first; bsdgames rot13 < second; else tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m' < empty; tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m' < first; tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m' < second; fi
